name: pdk-dbtplyr-dbt
instr:
We load the ops team's weekly store survey into dbt as a seed (quote_columns on) and build reports on it with dbtplyr, which is checked out in /app. The headers are whatever people type into the spreadsheet; the last two exports are in /data/exports. Since we switched, the select helpers pick up columns they shouldn't, some selections don't compile, and models built with across() either fail or show numbers that aren't in the export.

Every column of the export has to work, whatever its name. starts_with, ends_with, contains, not_contains, one_of and not_one_of should treat their text as plain text, ignoring case as they do now, and not_contains and not_one_of should return exactly the columns contains and one_of leave out. matches() keeps taking a regular expression. All of them should keep returning the stored names in the table's column order.

In across, c_across, if_any and if_all, `{{var}}` has to refer to that column. Where `{{var}}` touches letters, digits or underscores, as in `sum({{var}}) as {{var}}_tot` or `max_{{var}}`, the result is one column, e.g. `Revenue (USD)_tot`. `s.{{var}}` has to keep working. When an export adds columns, `dbt build --full-refresh` should give the same tables as a fresh build on it.

Nothing should change for plain lower case names, and `dbt build` in /app/integration_tests has to keep passing on its current seeds, which stay as they are. The project stays SQL: only SQL models, macros and YAML, with no Python models. There's no network;
